key_big: To a smaller unit, multiply. To a larger unit, divide. 1 m² = 10,000 cm².

body_html:
How it works

Metric units: 1 km = 1,000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 kg = 1,000 g, 1 litre = 1,000 ml. To change to a smaller unit, multiply; to a larger unit, divide.

Area and volume units are different: 1 m² = 10,000 cm² and 1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³. 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre.

A scale of 1 : 50,000 means 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm (500 m) in real life.

Example

Convert 3.5 kg into grams.

Multiply by 1,000.

Answer: 3,500 g

Example

Convert 2.5 m² into cm².

Multiply by 10,000.

Answer: 25,000 cm²

Example

On a 1 : 25,000 map, two places are 6 cm apart. Find the real distance.

6 × 25,000 = 150,000 cm.

÷ 100,000 for km.

Answer: 1.5 km

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying when you should divide: 2,500 g is 2.5 kg, not 2,500,000 kg.
  • Using 100 for every conversion: there are 1,000 m in a km and 1,000 g in a kg.
  • Using 100 for cm² to m². It is 10,000.
  • Leaving a map distance in cm instead of converting to m or km.

faq.q: How many cm² are in a m²?
faq.a: 10,000, because 1 m² is 100 cm by 100 cm.

faq.q: How do I use a map scale?
faq.a: Multiply the map distance by the scale number, then convert the answer from cm to m or km.

faq.q: How many cm³ make a litre?

faq.a: 1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm, 1 foot ≈ 30 cm, 5 miles ≈ 8 km, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb and 1 gallon ≈ 4.5 litres.
